note: Closed value lists for feed contract v2. Each value has a one-line meaning; basis names the doctrine or standard it follows. Version 1.1 (kit 0.6.0, contract revision 2.1) adds last_change, event_time_precision, place_basis, signal_tail, health_state and contract_rev.

values.observation: Something measured or reported, with no judgment about what it means.
values.assessment: A judgment about what is happening now or what it means.
values.forecast: A judgment about what will happen, with a resolution rule Verdict can score.

tier.basis: Grabo; NATO indicators versus indications; JP 2-0 warning

values.anomaly: Measured and outside the baseline. A measurement, not a warning.
values.warning: Judged. Carries likelihood, confidence, alternatives and what would change it.

tier.rev_2_1: Revision 2.1 meaning of anomaly (18 Nov 2026, D5): an observation of a subject that has not ended, outside that subject's own history (a series beyond a threshold on its own rolling baseline, flagged on no more than 5% of baseline readings; or an event or notice that is new or raised to the program's stated level within its hold, 72 hours unless stated), with the numbers in the item. Each program adopts it as its own method version; the one-line meaning above is rewritten at revision 2.2. See docs/feed-contract-v2.md.

values.update: Replaces the item named in supersedes.
values.cancel: Withdraws the item named in supersedes.
values.error: Corrects a mistaken issue named in supersedes.

values.exercise: Part of a training range or replay.
values.test: Pipeline test; never shown as live.

human_review.basis: ICD 505 labelling idea, applied to automated output

values.none: Fully automated, rule-based; no person looked at it before release.
values.sampled: A person reviews a sample of items from this method version.
values.full: A person reviewed this item before release.

indicator_state.basis: Grabo; the suite rule that missing data never means quiet

values.present: The indicator's condition is met in this period.
values.absent: Data arrived and the condition is not met.
values.no_data: Data did not arrive or did not cover enough of the area. Drawn grey; never read as absent.

direction.basis: CIA Tradecraft Primer (2009) indicators and signposts

values.changed: Changed in a way that is not up or down (scope, place, wording).
values.withdrawn: The prior judgment no longer stands.

values.assessed: Reached by this suite's own method from measurements or several independent sources.
values.reported: Reported by an independent outlet or agency; not measured by the suite.
values.claimed: A single-source or party claim. Drawn hollow; never moves a ladder on its own.

values.point: Location as published, to about 1 km.
values.area: A published polygon or the suite's own grid cell.
values.none: No location (for example a software vulnerability). Drawn off-map.

data_as_of_precision.basis: ISO 8601 reduced precision; suite display rule for sources that give no time (15 Nov 2026)

values.day: The source gives the date only. data_as_of is midnight UTC on that date; show the date, never a time or a zone.
values.month: The source gives the month only. data_as_of is midnight UTC on the 1st; show the month and year, never a day or a time.

product_category.basis: JP 2-0 intelligence products by purpose, adapted

values.estimative: Estimate or outlook: probabilistic and scored by Verdict.
values.baseline: Baseline or profile page (general military intelligence-like).

us_person_data.basis: A label, not a restriction (30 Oct 2026). The programs are not bound by the US intelligence community's limits on US-person information; a consumer that is (for example a government user) filters on this field and strips what its own rules require. US persons are US citizens, permanent residents, US-incorporated companies and associations made up substantially of citizens or permanent residents (FISA, 50 U.S.C. 1801(i); the intelligence community's rules define them the same way in substance).

values.none: Names no person or organization (counts, measurements, places).
values.organizations: Names organizations, which may include US companies or other US organizations.
values.individuals: Names or identifies individuals, who may be US persons (it may name organizations too).

ease_of_faking.basis: Heuer, Psychology of Intelligence Analysis, ch. 8

values.low: Hard to fake (physical measurement from several sensors).
values.medium: Possible to fake with effort (single sensor, official statement).
values.high: Easy to fake (social media post, unverified image, single claim).

contract_rev.basis: Additive revisions of tic-feed/2 (18 Nov 2026, D1): the contract string stays tic-feed/2

values.2.0: The contract as it stood to kit 0.5.12.
values.2.1: Kit 0.6.0: optional last_change, event times, subject_id, signal, sea_areas, place_basis and a documented health member; tightened data_as_of, countries and anomaly.

last_change.basis: Feed contract revision 2.1, F1 (18 Nov 2026, D2). State is tier and response_stage, as in the history log

values.new: The subject or condition first appeared.
values.raised: Its level moved up on its own ladder or across its own threshold.
values.lowered: Its level moved down on its own ladder or back across its own threshold.
values.changed: Scope, place or wording changed, with the level the same.
values.ended: No longer observed or in force.
values.none: No change in the program's record: standing for as long as the program has watched.

event_time_precision.basis: ISO 8601 reduced precision, as data_as_of_precision (feed contract revision 2.1, F2)

values.hour: The source gives the hour only. event_start and event_end sit on the hour; each covers its whole hour.
values.day: The source gives the date only. event_start and event_end are midnight UTC; each covers its whole day. Show dates, never times.
values.month: The source gives the month only. event_start and event_end are midnight UTC on the 1st; each covers its whole month.

place_basis.basis: Feed contract revision 2.1, F5 (18 Nov 2026, D7): why the item names these countries

values.location: It is, or it happened, there.
values.subject: The item is about that country (an advisory, a currency, a sanctions list), wherever it is.
values.named: A party is named: a victim's country, a network's home, an operator's origin. A join by place skips it.
values.zone: The program's own multi-country zone; counts as one place, not as each country in it.

signal_tail.basis: Feed contract revision 2.1, F4 (18 Nov 2026, D6): which direction of signal.value is unusual

values.high: Unusually high values are the departure.
values.low: Unusually low values are the departure.

health_state.basis: Watchfloor's feed health, the kit's source health (health.py); feed contract revision 2.1, F6 (18 Nov 2026, D8)

values.fresh: Read on this run; its newest data are inside the expected cadence.
values.late: Read on this run; its newest data are older than one cadence and inside two.
values.stale: Answering, but its newest data are older than two cadences: its items are withheld or drawn grey.
values.failing: The last read failed (error, timeout, empty answer). Never read as quiet.
values.never: Never read successfully, or no probe is defined.
values.up: Read on this run; it gives no time to judge freshness by.

corroboration_state.basis: Feed contract revision 2.1, F7 (18 Nov 2026, D11): reported, then corroborated

values.reported: One origin so far, or only the party's own claim: not yet corroborated.
values.corroborated: Two independent origins, or one official source speaking within its own remit.

values.origins: Two or more independent origins (wire copies and near-identical texts are one origin; one government's outlets are one origin).
values.official: The issuer speaking about its own remit: UKMTO for incidents it logs, an embassy for its own alert, an agency for its own measurement. An official about someone else's action is a party claim.
